title: Cagrilintide guide: how it works, the trial doses, CagriSema, and the diabetes medicines around it
excerpt: Every cagrilintide guide on this site in one place, arranged by topic: how the amylin analogue works, the doses its trials used, CagriSema, the new weight-loss drugs, and the diabetes medicines it would join.
body:
Cagrilintide is a once-weekly amylin analogue from Novo Nordisk. On its own it reduced body weight by up to 10.8% over 26 weeks in its dose-finding phase 2 trial [[1]], and combined with semaglutide as CagriSema it reduced weight by about 20% over 68 weeks in adults without diabetes [[2]] and by about 14% in adults with type 2 diabetes [[3]]. It is not approved anywhere yet.

This index lists every guide in the series. Each topic has one main guide and shorter guides underneath it that go deeper on one question. For the record itself, with every study, its tier and its source, start with the cagrilintide compound record. For the combination, the CagriSema record is the main guide of its topic, and the head-to-head arms are on cagrilintide vs semaglutide.

sections.heading: How this guide is organised
sections.html:
The guides follow one rule: a page answers one question, and it says plainly when the answer is that nothing has been established. Doses appear only as what trials administered, never as advice, and every number carries a numbered source mark that links straight to the paper or label it came from.

The three levels of the guide
LevelWhat it isWhere to find it
IndexThis page: every topic and every guideLinked from every guide's breadcrumb
Topic guideThe main guide for one topic, linking every guide beneath itThe bold link under each topic below
In-depth guideOne question, answered in full, with its sourcesThe cards under each topic

The diabetes guides are wider than cagrilintide on purpose. Amylin drugs are being developed for type 2 diabetes as well as for weight, and the questions people ask about them sit next to questions about the medicines they would join, from metformin and insulin to SGLT2 inhibitors like Jardiance.
